mnemonic: A stunt rider is asked whether he can clear the canyon. He gives a thumbs-up — "dâi" — the same sound as DIE, which is exactly what the crowd behind him expects. He can, and he does. Dâi is the can, the got, the managed-it. (↓ falling, the thumb comes down as the engine opens up)
scene: A helmeted stunt rider on a motorbike balanced at the lip of a wide desert canyon, giving a confident thumbs-up back over his shoulder to a small crowd of horrified onlookers with their hands on their heads.

mnemonic: A SWAT team smashes through the door, rifles up — then the lead officer lowers his weapon, presses his palms together and says softly, "sa-WAT-dee." The whole squad copies him. Even a raid starts with hello. (— levels out flat and calm on dee)
scene: A man presses both palms together in front of his chest and bows his head in a respectful greeting. He wears black tactical armour and a helmet. Behind him three more armoured figures fill a smashed doorway.

mnemonic: A man backing out of a café swings his bag into a waiter and a whole rack of toast goes up in the air. On the sill a crow caws. Caw, toast. He turns round with both hands raised, wincing, saying it twice over: khǎaw-thôot. (↑ khǎaw climbs like the crow, then thôot drops as he bows)
scene: The doorway of a small café. A man in a raincoat has just knocked a waiter's tray and slices of toast hang in the air around them both. He is turned back toward the waiter, shoulders hunched, both hands raised in apology, face screwed up.

mnemonic: A boy at the breakfast table tips the entire jar of orange Tang powder into one glass — not some of it, the lot. Tʰáng is the whole thing, both halves, every last one. (▲ high and taut, the voice stays up like the upended jar)
scene: A kitchen table at breakfast. A boy holds an enormous jar upside down over a single tall glass, orange powder pouring out and clouding the air around him. Cereal bowls forgotten. Morning light, curtains, an unimpressed cat on a chair.

mnemonic: A phone call in the middle of a market: where are you? The answer is one flat low word — yùu — and an arm goes straight up above the crowd so the caller can see where he is. yùu is being somewhere. (▁ low and flat, the voice sits still like the man)
scene: A crowded night market seen from slightly above. One man stands motionless among the moving crowd with a phone to his ear and his free arm raised straight up, waving. Everyone else is blurred with movement. String lights, food steam.

mnemonic: The vendor names a price so small that the shopper has already walked off with the shirt. It took almost nothing. Thùuk is cheap — and, awkwardly for the learner, also correct. (▁ low and flat, a short blunt word for a short blunt price)
scene: A clothes stall in a covered market. A shopper walks away with a folded shirt under his arm, already several steps gone, while the vendor stands with one open palm holding a single small coin. Hanging garments, strip lights, crowded aisle.

mnemonic: A woman comes to her back door and finds a hen where no hen should be: up on the kitchen table, mid-strut, among the breakfast plates. Her chin lifts as she says it — hěn, I see it. (↑ rising, the voice climbs with the eyebrows)
scene: A kitchen seen from the back doorway. A brown hen stands on the table stepping between plates and a teapot. A woman in the doorway has stopped dead, hands still on the door frame, chin up. Morning light across the floor tiles.

mnemonic: Given a mountain of vegetables to get through, the chef grins and reaches for the cleaver — chop, chop, chop, all afternoon — because this is the part of the job she likes. Chɔ̂ɔp is liking a thing enough to choose it. (↓ falling, the blade comes down with the voice)
scene: A restaurant prep kitchen. A chef mid-swing with a heavy cleaver over a board heaped with spring onions, a vast crate of vegetables beside her, grinning. Chopped piles fan out across the steel counter. Steam and hard kitchen light.

mnemonic: A fortune teller peers over her cards, jabs a finger across the table and says "Ah — YOU!" She has guessed your age to the year, and the YOU comes out bright and hard and stays up there. aa-yú is the number of years you have. (▲ the second syllable snaps up high on YOU and holds)
scene: A fortune teller's booth draped in red cloth. An old woman with rings on every finger leans across a spread of cards and jabs one finger directly at the viewer, eyes wide with certainty.

mnemonic: The hunter presses his ear flat to the coffin lid with the fangs an inch away on the other side. Listening is the entire job. Fang is to listen, and it is the English word unchanged. (— flat and level, held completely still)
scene: A stone crypt lit by one candle. A man kneels with his ear pressed against the lid of a heavy wooden coffin, eyes wide, both palms flat on the wood. Cobwebs, damp walls, a single flame.

mnemonic: One hen finds the split feed sack and immediately tells the whole yard about it — bawk, bawk, bawk — until every bird in the place is running. Bɔ̀ɔk is to tell: news, instructions, or the truth. (▁ low and flat, a plain announcement)
scene: A farmyard. One hen stands on a burst sack of grain with her beak open mid-squawk, wings half spread, while a dozen other hens sprint toward her from every corner. Spilled feed, straw, hard morning light.

mnemonic: Four friends outside a karaoke bar and one of them still hesitating on the step. The others tug his sleeve: pai thə̀ — go on, let's. It is the softest possible shove, the syllable that turns an order into a let's. (▁ low and short, gone almost before it starts)
scene: A neon karaoke doorway at night. Three young people have hold of a fourth by the sleeve and elbow, hauling him laughing toward the entrance while he leans back. Wet pavement, reflected neon, scooters parked along the kerb.

mnemonic: A single yen coin has been left in the freezer overnight and comes out furred with white frost, so cold it sticks to the fingertips that lift it. yen is cold, and the temperature never shifts while the voice holds it. (— flat and level, the cold does not move)
scene: A close view of a hand holding a small coin, its face lost under white frost, fingertips pink and stuck to its surface, cold vapour spilling down from an open freezer behind.

mnemonic: The twin of หน่อย, but the voice stays up high. A boy holds the bag upside down over his palm: one chilli left, nɔ́ɔi, that is all there is. (▲ high and taut, held up like the chilli itself)
scene: A boy holding a nearly empty paper bag upside down over his open palm with a single small red chilli sitting in it, arm raised so a woman at a stove can see.

mnemonic: Two people stand in front of a canvas of splashes with their heads tilted. It might be art. It might not. Àat is exactly that hedge — may, might, possibly — said like 'art' with the R swallowed. (▁ low and flat, no commitment in the voice)
scene: A white gallery wall with one enormous splattered canvas. Two visitors stand well back with their heads tilted at the same angle, one with a hand on his chin. Spotlights, polished concrete floor.

mnemonic: A small boy has claimed the rail at the stern of the ferry and is shouting at the wake. The deck is his. Dèk is a child — short, blunt and low, like the boards under his feet. (▁ low and flat, a short stamp of a word)
scene: The stern deck of a wooden ferry. A small boy grips the rail and leans out over the churning white wake, mouth open, hair flat in the wind. Passengers sit behind him in the shade. Bright glare off the water.

mnemonic: Ràp, to receive, is sitting inside it: sǎm-ràp marks whoever receives the thing. A boy hands over a brown-paper parcel wrapped for a man named Sam — Sam-rap — and it is for him, nobody else. (▁ the second syllable drops low, the parcel changes hands)
scene: A boy on a doorstep holding out a brown-paper parcel tied with string to a man who has both hands on it. Neither has let go. Terrace houses, milk bottles on the step, flat morning light.

mnemonic: Slip a vowel into the middle of 'smart' and you have sǎa-mâat — and smart is exactly what it means: able to do the thing. A woman crouches at a dead fuse box and brings the stall back to life with a hairpin. (↓ falls on the second syllable, the job done)
scene: A night market stall gone dark while the ones either side blaze. A woman crouches at an open fuse box with a hairpin between her fingers, the vendor holding a torch over her shoulder. Cables, crates, curious faces.

mnemonic: The toddler's first word finally comes and the whole room stops dead. Kham sounds like 'come' and means word: one word, the unit you count them in. (— flat and level, a small even sound)
scene: A living room. A toddler stands holding the edge of a chair with her mouth open mid-sound, and four adults around the room have frozen mid-movement, all turned toward her. Tea going cold, afternoon light.

mnemonic: The man at the back of the queue has the longest wait of anybody. Lǎng is behind — the back of a thing, and after in time. Long queue, back of it, both in one word. (↑ rising, the voice climbs as he cranes to see the front)
scene: An enormous queue snaking twice around a government building. The last man in line stands on tiptoe craning to see the distant front, bag on the ground at his feet. Hot sun, concrete, hundreds of shoulders.

mnemonic: The father word with the drop taken out: pʰɔ̂ɔ is dad, pʰɔɔ is enough. His enormous paw goes flat over the top of the glass before anyone can pour more. Same paw, level voice. (— flat and level, no drop at all)
scene: A dinner table. A big weathered hand lies flat across the mouth of a glass while a bottle tips toward it and stops. Plates pushed back, other hands resting on the cloth. Warm evening light.

mnemonic: She lifts a tiny gold ring off the velvet and the jeweller calmly builds the stack of banknotes it will cost beside it, a stack taller than the ring is wide. The pang goes straight through her chest. phaaeng: expensive. (— flat and level, the price is not negotiable)
scene: A jeweller's counter under bright spotlights. A small gold ring sits on a velvet pad; beside it the jeweller has built a tall stack of banknotes. The customer has one hand pressed flat to her chest, leaning back, eyes wide.

mnemonic: The doctor tips a spoonful of syrup into the boy and, before he has finished swallowing, is already filling the spoon again. More. More rest, more water, more of this. mǎaw is the doctor, and more is what she always wants. (↑ rising, the voice lifts with the spoon)
scene: A small clinic room. A doctor in a white coat with a stethoscope round her neck holds a brimming spoon of dark syrup toward a boy on the examination couch, the bottle in her other hand already tilted to refill it.

mnemonic: The lifeboat is going down by the stern, so over the side go the suitcases, the chairs, the oars, everything. What he will not let go of is one dented tin can of water held hard against his chest. Some can. sǎm-khan is the thing that actually matters. (↑ sǎm climbs, then khan lands flat and certain)
scene: An overloaded wooden lifeboat low in a grey swell. A man at the stern heaves a suitcase over the side with one arm while the other clamps a dented tin can tight against his chest. Other passengers cling to the gunwales, soaked.

mnemonic: Mum points, arm dead straight, at the place where the two walls meet, and the boy goes and stands in it. That exact meeting of two walls is the mum: the corner, the angle. Nobody argues with the arm. (— flat and level, no rise, no give)
scene: A plain sitting room. A woman stands with her arm extended rigidly toward the corner where two walls meet; a small boy trudges toward it with his head down and one sock falling. Afternoon light through net curtains, an armchair pushed aside.

mnemonic: The doctor asks which one is hurting and he smacks his own knee twice, hard: nîi. This one. Not that one, not the one from last year, this knee, the one he can reach and hit. นี่ always points at whatever is nearest to hand. (↓ falling, the voice drops with the hand)
scene: A clinic examination room. A man sitting on the couch with both trouser legs rolled up slaps his own left knee with a flat palm, caught mid-strike, jaw set. The doctor leans in with a small torch, eyebrows up.

mnemonic: Yin is the female half of the old pair. Finish it the way English finishes sing and you have jǐŋ, the word for female. A dancer turns slowly out of the light and into the dark, half bright and half shadow, all in one movement. (↑ rising, the voice climbs with the turn)
scene: A dark stage. A Thai dancer in a gold headdress and long silk skirt turns slowly mid-movement, her curved fingers and the sweep of her skirt tracing a circle; one half of her lit warm, the other lost in shadow.

mnemonic: A small son stands at the chai stall with his mouth open, following the long ribbon of tea as the vendor pours it from a pot held high into one held low. He has forgotten his own cup entirely. Son, chai: sǒn-jai is exactly that, your attention gone somewhere else. (↑ sǒn climbs, then jai lands flat where his eyes are)
scene: A street chai stall at dusk. A vendor pours a long ribbon of milky tea from a pot held high into another held low, steam curling off it.

mnemonic: Ben swings round with a glass of rye and puts the whole thing down your front. You look at the stain, look at Ben, and wave it away: mâi-bpen-rai. My, Ben, rye. Never mind, it is nothing, it is okay. (↓ mâi drops hard, then the last two float off flat)
scene: A crowded wooden bar. A man has just turned with a tumbler and sloshed dark spirit down the front of another man's shirt; the glass is still tipped in his hand, his face frozen in horror. The soaked man is laughing, one hand raised palm out, entirely unbothered.

mnemonic: Take ANGRY and stop it dead with a t: ang-grìt. A bowler-hatted man stands in the rain glaring at a cup of tea gone stone cold, furious and entirely silent about it. That is England. (▁ the second syllable drops low and stops short)
scene: A grey wet street. A man in a bowler hat and long dark coat stands under a black umbrella, rain sheeting off it, glaring down at a cup and saucer balanced on a low wall in front of him, his face red with contained fury.

mnemonic: Three children are digging up the vegetable patch and the noise is tremendous: spades ringing on stone, shrieking, black earth going over the fence. A din. And din is the very stuff they are throwing about, the soil itself. (— flat and level, said as plainly as the ground)
scene: A back garden vegetable patch churned into a crater. Three children with spades fling dark crumbly soil over their shoulders, mouths open in shrieks, earth hanging in the air around them. A dog barks at the edge of the hole.

mnemonic: Take QUALM and drop the m: kʰwǎa. At the fork she gets a qualm about it, hangs there a full second with both hands locked on the wheel — and then swings right anyway. The doubt lives in the sound; the turn is the meaning. (↑ rising, the voice lifts like the question she is asking herself)
scene: A car stopped at a rural fork. The driver, hands tense on the wheel, looks down the right-hand branch with a worried frown while the front wheels begin to bite that way. Lone tree, flat afternoon light.

mnemonic: โรง is the building — the same โรง that sits in cinema, hotel and factory — and เรียน is to learn. Put the hall and the learning together and school falls out of it: roong-riian, the learning hall. Take โรง away with you; it builds half a town. (— both syllables level and even, like a held bell)
scene: A school courtyard at morning assembly. Rows of children in white shirts and navy shorts stand in the dust facing a long low building with an open verandah, hands at their sides. A teacher stands at the front with one arm raised.

mnemonic: A phone lies face down in a puddle in the middle of the road, ringing and ringing while the rain hammers it flat, and nobody is coming for it. fǒn is that rain, and the voice climbs the way a ring tone does. (↑ rising, the pitch lifts like a phone waiting to be answered)
scene: A tarmac road in a downpour, seen low and close. A mobile phone lies face down in a shallow puddle, rain bouncing off its back in bright crowns. The street beyond dissolves into grey water and blurred headlights.

mnemonic: At dawn a woman kneels and spoons rice into a monk's bowl, and he will thaan it. Where kin is blunt and everyday, thaan is the soft, polite word for eat — the one you use for a guest, an elder, a monk. (— flat and level, gently said)
scene: Dawn on a Thai street. A woman kneels barefoot on the pavement spooning rice into the alms bowl of a monk in saffron robes, his eyes lowered and head bowed; a line of monks waits behind him in the mist.

mnemonic: ผู้ is the one-who, the same ผู้ that starts the words for man and woman, and ใหญ่ is big. An adult is simply the big one: the person who takes the jar off the top shelf without going up on anything. phûu-yài. (↓ phûu drops, then yài settles low, with the weight of being the big one)
scene: A kitchen. A small girl up on tiptoe on a stool strains toward a plain jar on the highest shelf, fingers short of it by a foot.
